posts.body: Buyer's agent ghosted mid-transaction last week. Inspection to close in ten days. Deal almost died because one person checked out. That's when I realized something. You can't build a real business around agents who vanish when things get hard. You need people who show up. Period.

I spent two years telling agents that higher splits would make them happy. Paid out 80.20 splits. Watched them leave anyway. Then I stopped and asked the ones staying what actually kept them around.

It wasn't the commission. They said it was the same thing every time. I picked up when they called. We solved problems together. They didn't feel like they were running a solo business out of a brokerage office.

That's when it clicked. Most brokers have it backwards. They think agents leave for better splits. The real reason agents leave is because nobody's there.

I've talked to agents at big national brokers. They have lower splits than us. They have better technology. They still feel invisible.

The split doesn't matter if you're alone when a deal falls apart at 9pm.

Are you still convinced the commission structure at your current brokerage is actually what's keeping you there?

We're running with more buyer and lease leads than we can properly work right now. Mostly new construction in San Antonio and Austin, plus out-of-state relocations looking to move to Texas.

1. These leads are warm but they're not ready today. They need vetting and nurture before they're conversion ready. That's the honest part.

2. If you're built for lead follow-up and patient with pipeline building, this is real volume. Not quick closings. Real opportunity.

3. This isn't about taking every lead that comes through the door. It's about agents who know how to work warm prospects into actual deals.

If this sounds like something you'd take on, send me a DM.

You're grinding through a market that doesn't feel like it's moving. Three months between deals. Leads that go cold. The phone quiet on days it shouldn't be. You start wondering if you picked the wrong career or the wrong time to pick it.

Here's what I know. Every agent making real money right now went through exactly this. They didn't quit. They didn't blame the market. They stayed consistent when consistency felt pointless. They kept showing up when showing up looked stupid from the outside.

The market doesn't care about your doubt. It rewards the agent who's still working when everyone else stopped. That's not motivational poster talk. That's just how it works.

Your bet on yourself right now matters more than the market. Stay in it.

If you want to talk about what we're building at Lifestyle Design Realty, send me a DM.

Had a listing fall apart Tuesday. Inspection found foundation issues the seller didn't disclose. Buyer's lender killed it in hours. Thought we were done.

1. The agent didn't panic. Called me. We walked through three scenarios instead of one. That matters.

2. We pivoted to cash buyers before the listing went stale. Found two legitimate offers by Thursday. One closed.

3. The real win wasn't saving the deal. It was that the agent had someone to call who knew what to do when the obvious path disappeared.

Most agents sit alone with problems like this and watch deals die. They tell themselves it's the market or the buyer or bad luck.

When's the last time you had someone to actually call when a deal went sideways?

Most agents think they need to chase more leads. What they actually need is to stop working with leads that were never going to close anyway.

You know the ones. They inquiry. They ghost for two weeks. They come back with unrealistic expectations. They waste your mental energy. I spent years thinking volume solved everything. More leads meant more deals. What I didn't track was how many of those leads actually converted versus how many just cluttered my pipeline and made me feel busy instead of productive. The agents doing real numbers aren't necessarily seeing more prospects. They're qualifying harder upfront and walking away from the bad ones faster. That one change cuts your workload in half and doubles your close rate.

If you want to talk about what we're building at Lifestyle Design Realty, send me a DM.

You're outgrowing your current situation and you don't want to admit it yet.

You're closing deals consistently. Your split might even be decent. But you're solving problems alone. Your broker doesn't know your name. There's no one pushing you to think bigger or showing you how to scale beyond the daily grind. You're capable of more and the people around you aren't built to help you get there. That gap between where you are and where you could be keeps getting wider. At some point you stop wondering if you should move and start wondering why you haven't already.

What would it take for you to actually make the move?
